children: Shares of Target Hospitality fell after the company launched and priced an underwritten secondary offering.
The stock declined 6.4% to $18.96 in premarket trading on Wednesday. Shares had more than doubled year to date at market close.
The accommodations and hospitality services provider said the upsized offering of 14 million shares is now priced at $18.50 per share.
The company had initially expected an offering of 13 million shares.

The company said it expects the selling stockholders--which include Arrow Holdings S.a r.l. and MFA Global S.a r.l.--to get about $259 million in total gross proceeds from the offering. It expects the offering to close Sept. 10.
The selling stockholders have granted underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 2.1 million shares.

With the completion of the offering, the company plans to purchase up to $30 million in shares of its common stock from the underwriters, at the same price paid by the underwriters to the selling stockholders in the offering, using cash on hand and borrowings under a credit facility. The company said it expects to hold those shares as treasury shares.
